extracted.intended_audience: physicians and medical professionals (readers of professional/medical commentary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for professional conduct in medicine focused on identifying, resisting, and not legitimizing medical 'systems', cures, and charlatanry; also includes related professional-scientific standards illustrated by exemplary scientific practice. Aimed at encouraging scientific integrity and transparent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of 'systems' and proprietary 'cures' in medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: There can not possibly be a 'system' or 'cure' in medicine. The art of healing is not a system, and can never be made one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medicine should not be treated as a closed system or set of dogmatic rules; systems and 'cures' that claim a unified formula for healing are incompatible with honest scientific practice. The profession must refuse recognition of such systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use remedies only with knowledge of their nature and action
rubrics_metrics.description: If we do not know what a remedy is, and how it acts, we have no right, as honest men, to employ it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians must only employ treatments whose constituents and mechanisms are understood; employing nostrums or unexplained remedies is unprofessional and constitutes quackery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational study and treatment on common-sense principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Our calling consists solely in the rational study and treatment of disease on common-sense principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnosis and treatment should be grounded in rational investigation of symptoms, causes, and drug actions rather than in mysticism or inspirational claims; apply observation, analysis, and reasoned methods in clinical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test drugs and methods by careful trial and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: We test the powers and analyze the constitution of drugs, and we scrutinize and make careful trial of methods of treatment, to obtain a reasonable acquaintance with their natures and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapies must be subjected to scrutiny, experiment, and repeated trial to learn their effects; clinicians should analyze pharmacology and evaluate treatments empirically rather than by faith or tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profession must publicly and promptly oppose quackery
rubrics_metrics.description: The profession must speak out clearly and strongly on this point, and without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical practitioners and institutions have an obligation to denounce charlatanry and not to tacitly endorse systems or dubious remedies; silence or polite indulgence aids quackery and harms public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay aside mystery; be candid and transparent with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: We must lay aside the last vestige of the robe of mystery, and show by our words and works, our conduct and policy, that medicine is not a science that admits of inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mystifying language, secrecy, or appeals to inspiration; cultivate openness about methods, limits of knowledge, and rational bases for treatments to maintain public confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No professional endorsement of 'inspirational' practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: For those who pretend to a sort of inspiration we have no professional friendship; and toward the promoters of systems and 'pathies we can have no leaning, or any feeling other than that of suspicion, if not pity and contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not socialize professionally with or endorse those who claim supernatural or unscientific bases for medical practice; regard promoters of such systems with suspicion and refrain from giving them legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject rule-of-thumb and mysterious methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no rule-of-thumb methods and no mysteries in true science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical decisions should not be based on arbitrary heuristics or secretive practices; adopt scientific standards and reproducible methods instead of anecdote-driven shortcuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal and institutional commitment to uncompromising scientific sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is so much needed just now as the rise in our midst of a stern and uncompromising apostle of sincerity in science — a man of unpitying animosity to humbug in all its forms, who will not hesitate, at any bidding, to denounce wrong-doing and untruthfulness, let who may be the offender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals and professional bodies should cultivate and reward frank, uncompromising critique of fraudulent or deceptive practices, even when politically or socially difficult; integrity should trump tact that shelters quackery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not patronize or encourage quackery by professional credulity
rubrics_metrics.description: We pander to the credulity of the unskilled community when we show ourselves credulous. We patronize and encourage quackery when we extend professional recognition to a quack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving public or professional legitimacy to unproven treatments or practitioners; professional endorsement (even tacit) fuels public belief in ineffective or harmful remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway block-safety protocol (illustrative procedural standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A railway section must allow only one train at a time; the sending station issues a two-beat warning twice to indicate 'a train is coming,' which is acknowledged by one beat; the sending station sends two beats to tell the other that 'the train is in'; the receiving station raises a semaphore behind the train to prevent another from being sent and acknowledges with one beat; after the train has arrived the receiving station sends three beats to indicate 'Line clear' and lower the semaphore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow explicit, reproducible signal sequences and mutual acknowledgements before permitting another train to enter a section; do not send another train until explicit confirmation of arrival and 'line clear' has been received — an example of strict procedural safety and mutual verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific practice: precision, method, and publication (exemplary standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific work should be precise and methodical: use new technologies (e.g., electricity for longitude determination, photographic processes), take repeated independent observations (e.g., magnitude determined by not less than four independent observations), improve instruments, and publish data and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt technological innovation to improve measurement, insist on multiple independent observations to ensure reliability, refine instrumentation, and disseminate findings through publication to advance the field and allow verification.
